name: Elements of Corporate Worship (Word, Sacrament, Prayer)

objectives.text: Identify the main things God's people do when they gather for worship, such as hearing the Bible, praying, and singing
Name the sermon as the part of worship when the pastor explains God's Word to the congregation
Recall that Christians gather together on the Lord's Day to worship God as one church family
Describe what the congregation does during the public reading of Scripture in worship
Recite the Aaronic blessing and identify it as words from Scripture used to bless God's people in worship
Explain the pattern of worship in which God speaks to His people through His Word and they respond with prayer and praise
Identify the kinds of prayer offered in corporate worship, including praise, confession, thanksgiving, and intercession
Explain the purpose of the Call to Worship as God's summons that opens the gathered service
Explain how the Lord's Prayer serves as a pattern for the prayers of the congregation
Describe how baptism and the Lord's Supper take their place in corporate worship as visible signs of the promises proclaimed in the Word
Explain the purpose of congregational singing as praising God and teaching and admonishing one another
Explain the Benediction as God's blessing pronounced on His people at the close of worship
Explain how the offering functions as an act of worship in which God's people give thanks and support the ministry and the poor
Analyze why the reading and preaching of the Word stand at the center of Reformed corporate worship
Describe how the catechism directs a congregation to hear the preached Word with preparation, attention, and testing by Scripture
Analyze the function of the Confession of Sin and the Assurance of Pardon within the order of worship
Compare the elements of worship described in the early church with the elements of a present-day order of service
Explain the Westminster teaching that Word, sacraments, and prayer are the ordinary means of grace made effective by the Holy Spirit
Explain why the Westminster Confession directs that public prayer be made in the name of Christ, by the help of the Spirit, and in a known tongue
Analyze the Reformed teaching that the sacrament is joined to and depends on the preached Word of promise
Construct a scriptural explanation of why God gathers His people as an assembly to worship Him together
Compare Reformation changes to corporate worship, such as preaching and singing in the common language, with late medieval practice
Evaluate congregational songs by whether their words teach sound doctrine and serve the Word
Defend the necessity of preaching in corporate worship from Scripture and the Westminster standards
Analyze the order of a Reformed service as a pattern of covenant renewal moving from call and confession through Word and sacrament to blessing
Design an order of corporate worship and justify the purpose and placement of each element from Scripture

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (worship elements, sermon, gathering together, Scripture reading, dialogical pattern, Call to Worship, Benediction, offering, centrality of the Word, Confession and Assurance, ordinary means of grace, gathered assembly, music, preaching, covenant renewal). Dropped the private vs corporate prayer comparison as belonging to the Private Devotion sibling and kept sacrament coverage to its place in the service, leaving baptism and communion doctrine to that sibling. Moved the offering earlier. Added objectives on kinds of corporate prayer, the Lord's Prayer as a pattern, singing's purpose, hearing the preached Word, early church elements, Westminster directives on public prayer, Word and sacrament relationship, Reformation worship changes, and designing an order of worship. Recast the music objective around doctrinal content rather than feeling and replaced 1 Corinthians 16:2 and 1 John 1:9 with fuller verse ranges and added confessional anchors.
